t: Options rebuilt: five tabs (Graphics, Controls, Audio, Game, System) with proper switches, segmented choices and sliders that show their real value, and a hint under every setting. Held sideways on a phone the tabs sit in a rail on the left so the settings get the full height.
One reload for all graphics changes: settings that rebuild the renderer are marked, saved, and applied together with one Apply & reload bar, instead of reloading the game after every tap.

Graphics presets (Performance / Balanced / Quality) set quality, anti-aliasing, sky lighting and auto resolution in one tap, and show Custom when you have changed one of them. Reset all options is in the System tab (two taps; your bikes and multiplayer name stay).

MSAA is back as an anti-aliasing choice next to FXAA: Off, FXAA, MSAA 2×, MSAA 4× or MSAA 4× + FXAA. It runs in the scene pass, so it works together with the colour grade and the N64 filter. WebGPU only has 4× samples (2× runs as 4×), and a GPU that cannot multisample falls back to FXAA and says so in Options. Your old FXAA on/off choice carries over.

Proper passengers on every bike, not just the tricycle: stop next to a friend's bike and tap their name tag (it shows 🏍️+1 when the pillion seat is free). RIDE asks, the driver taps OK, and you sit behind them. The passenger is the rider model again, shifted back onto the seat in different clothes (eight outfits, picked by player), so it costs one extra draw call and no new triangles.

The weight is real: 65 kg behind the rider moves the bike's centre of mass back and up, so it pulls away slower (a Raider 150 takes about 1.2 s longer to 60 km/h, a Smash 115 about 2.8 s), the front gets light and wheelies come earlier, braking distance is about the same. Taking the passenger off gives the bike back exactly.

First person looks over the driver's shoulder; GET OFF puts your own bike down on the driver's left. If the bike crashes, the passenger is flung out cartoon-style like the sidecar passengers. Switching bikes or fitting / removing the sidecar drops the passenger. A tricycle still seats two on the sidecar bench.
No relay update needed (the pillion uses the first entry of the same seat list). New: tools/pillion.mjs checks every bike's seat against the real model and plays a whole ride through a fake relay.

Cuter and lighter wheels: spokes, rim lip, hub, pinstripes and brake discs are now flat cut-out textures (N64 style) instead of little 3D parts. Every bike lost about 700-1,500 triangles (all eight together: 30.9k to 23.5k, a quarter of the bike geometry); the draw call count did not change.
The tyre is still a chunky 3D ring. The garage wheel colour, rim tape and carbon wheels still work, and brake discs now have drilled holes.
Faster: far fewer draw calls. Measured in five spots (lot, town, highway, town edge, plaza) on Medium: 115-180 draw calls per frame before, 26-35 now, with the same picture.

The ground is one object (every 280 m tile at every detail level, drawn nearest first), the roads are one per surface, and on WebGL 2 every prop of the island (houses, shops, roofs, trees, palms, poles, rails, parked vehicles, lamps...) is drawn once per material for the whole island instead of once per type per 700 m chunk. Untextured props and the church share one material, so most of the town is a single draw. All shadow-casting props are one draw in the shadow pass. Props now hide per 140 m cell instead of per 700 m chunk, so less off-screen geometry is drawn too.
Quest beacons are two draws in total (rings, beams) instead of 2-3 each; light pools are one, and pools and halos are skipped entirely by day (they were drawn invisible).
WebGPU keeps its GPU culling for props; the ground, roads, pools and beacons are batched there too. Not yet checked on a real phone.

Fixed: the mountain (terrace) road was buried. Where the road runs lower than the hillside, the grass climbed as a wall up to 17 m high within 5 m of the centre line, and the 5 m terrain mesh poked through the road surface, so the road was hard to see and you rode into invisible-looking walls. The ground beside a road now rises as a graded cut bank (at most 0.7 m per metre) behind a level shoulder, in bare earth colour so the road stands out against the grass, and no terrain reaches above the road surface any more.
Terrain below a road (embankments, bridges, river crossings) is unchanged. tools/roads.mjs now also checks the drawn mesh and the physics ground beside every road (CORRIDOR).

Fixed: bumps where roads meet. Every road used to be shaped on its own, so where two roads overlapped (crossings, branches, the town's north-east corner, the airstrip's taxi roads) they sat at different heights and the ground jumped between the two surfaces along the line where the nearest road changes: up to half a metre at the highway junctions. Now every junction is one level surface: the roads there share one height over the whole overlap and ease back into their own terrain-following profile at a gentle grade.
Fixed: the highway loop had a 6 cm step where its end met its start. It is now smoothed as a closed loop.
Fixed: a strip of ground inside a wide road could be treated as the shoulder of a narrower road next to it (a small lip). The road whose edge is nearest now decides.
The speed bumps are the only bumps left on the road: new tools/roads.mjs fails the test run if any junction, crossing or the loop seam has a step in it.

Fixed: the on-foot character was still drawn sitting down. The rider's parts are merged into one mesh when the bike is built, so the standing pose never kicked in. The body is now rebuilt standing (legs straight, torso upright, arms hanging) from the bike's own rider measurements.
On foot, first person: the walking bob is now Half-Life 1 style and much gentler: vertical only (no side sway, roll or wobble), one slow up-down per stride, height following your speed.

On foot, feel: the camera is much smoother (look angles ease, steps and slopes glide instead of popping, the third-person camera trails you softly and pulls back a little when you sprint), the body now stands upright instead of staying in the seated pose, and the first-person view has a proper walking bob, side sway and a faint breath when standing still.

On foot, movement: speed eases in and out with real friction instead of snapping, sprint builds up and drops off smoothly (with a slight widening of the view), turning around at speed is quick, and in first person backing up and strafing are slower. Jumping is more forgiving: you can still jump a moment after walking off an edge, a jump pressed just before landing counts, a tap is a short hop and holding the button jumps full height. Take-off and landing dip the camera, and a hard landing costs a little speed.
Fixed: KEY, KILL, START and BACK stayed on screen on touch devices while walking; they are now hidden whenever you are off the bike.
The main menu now has the garage look: dark frosted-glass panels, flat amber-highlight buttons and spaced amber headings. The island scene behind it is dimmed to match.
Fixed: the UPDATE button's version number was amber on amber and couldn't be read. (Menu theme by mrralphmc-ux, PR #1.)

Night lights: the light pools on the ground under lamp posts now follow the terrain (each pool is a small grid hugging the drawn ground) instead of a flat disc that floated over slopes and uneven ground.
On foot: CAM (or C) switches between first person (eyes at the helmet, no body) and third person.

On foot, touch controls: all the bike's controls are hidden and replaced by a joystick (push it all the way to run) and a JUMP button (hold to keep hopping); drag the screen to look around; GET OFF / GET ON now has its own free spot chosen by the layout solver, so it no longer sits on top of other buttons.

You can now get off the bike: F (or the GET OFF button when stopped) parks it with the key off and puts your rider on foot beside it. WASD walk, Shift run, Space jump, drag to look around; on touch the gas pad walks, the brake pad walks back, the wheel turns the camera and the up arrow jumps. You collide with buildings and the bike, can't wade into the sea, and F / GET ON next to the bike puts you back on it. Barebones for now: no animation, and other players still see your bike parked with its rider.
Fixed: the game didn't load in Firefox ("three" was not remapped).

Maps can now have extra islands, and every building is part of the map: roadside houses, nipa huts and shophouses are placed one by one, and the church, plaza, market, gas station and parking lot can be moved (the ground under them is levelled). Refuelling, parking quests and the spawn follow them.
The island's trees and palms were re-scattered once by this change.
The island is now loaded from swappable map files, ready for community-made map changes. Roads keep their own max grade when set.

Garage: the camera now frames the bike in the space the panels leave free (beside the panel in landscape, above it in portrait) and zooms to fit each bike's size, so the CBR, the scooters and the TMX with its tricycle sidecar are never cut off. Close-ups scale with the screen too; pinch / wheel zoom is relative.

Bike selection: the garage has a compact picker (‹ name ›, tap the name for a grid of all bikes) instead of rows of buttons. The title-screen bike list is a grid of cards with class, drivetrain, a power bar and weight.

Perf: the sun's shadow map is only redrawn when the light actually moves (it now follows the bike in ~3 m steps). Parked: no shadow pass at all; riding: a fraction of the frames. Shadows look the same.
Perf: GPU culling of the island props (trees, houses, posts...) is now one compute pass for all prop types instead of one per type, and is skipped entirely while the camera stands still.
Perf: all culling (distance, terrain detail, GPU props) now runs from one place each frame.
Fix: braking hard at speed could stand the bike on its nose and keep it there while the brake was held. The suspension now tops out, and lifting the rear wheel is left to the stoppie model.

Sound: silent layers (wind, tyre, brake, chain and ambience beds at zero volume) stop running on the audio thread until they are needed, and the engine voice idles when the engine is off or sound is muted. Less CPU and battery for the same sound.
Perf meter: cpu now reads game + draw time (e.g. 3.1+12.4 ms), and hitches caused by drawing are filed under draw instead of js.
New bike: Yamaha Aerox 155. 155 cc liquid-cooled VVA, 15.4 PS, CVT (2.300–0.724), 14" wheels, twin rear shocks, Stop & Start System.
New bike: Kawasaki Rouser NS125 Fi. 124 cc FI single, 12 PS, 5-speed, front disc / rear drum, 17" alloys, split seat.
New bike: Rusi Macho 125. 125 cc carb single, 9.7 hp, 5-speed, drum/drum, 17" spokes. Takes the tricycle sidecar in Parts.
Each new bike has its own sound profile (brakes, chain or belt, body rattle, starter).
New: WHAT'S NEW on the title screen shows these patch notes.
New: the game now checks for updates. When a newer build is out, an UPDATE button appears on the title screen and in the pause menu; one tap reloads into the new version (works with offline mode).
Tricycle rides: tap a trike's name tag (within 9 m, both stopped) to ask for a ride. Up to 2 passengers per trike, and each adds weight to the driver's physics.
Crashes fling passengers and the driver cartoon-style.
Sidecar windscreen is now transparent.
Multiplayer relay protocol update: ride messages need the relay redeployed.
New bike: TMX Supremo. 149 cc carb, 5-speed manual, drum brakes, 18" spoked wheels, twin-dial cluster.
Optional tricycle sidecar (Parts > Sidecar) with its own physics: no lean, pulls toward the sidecar on throttle, chair lift and rollover.
Fixed a frozen sound loop in the part sounds.
Part sounds: brake squeal, chain whirr and clunk, clutch rasp, suspension thump, body rattle, key clicks, exhaust ping, peg grind. Every bike has its own profile.
Grip-limited steering, wheelie control, smoother camera, regrip fix. Analog brake (11.4 - 11.6). Tyre model (11.2).
